clue.text: What may well be chewed over at meeting — money!

indicators.note: over tells us to turn the chewed stuff round, reading it backwards

parts.note: cud is what a cow chews over and over

explanation.surface: Someone at a meeting grumbles that money is what will be chewed over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' is the reversal sign and 'meeting' only joins the pieces. A ducat was an old gold coin used across Europe.
explanation.definitionFit: A ducat is an old European gold coin, so it is a form of cash.

clue.text: Paint can give rise to beastly ill-feeling

explanation.surface: A tin of paint is blamed for bad tempers.
explanation.walkthrough: Distemper is a cheap water-based paint, and also a disease of dogs and other animals; read playfully, DIS-TEMPER is bad temper, made 'beastly' by the animal sense.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a matt wall coating; the other is a viral illness of dogs, jokingly treated as an animal's bad mood.

clue.text: Outdoor wear right for spring

parts.note: a cape is a sleeveless cloak worn outside

explanation.surface: A recommendation of the right coat for springtime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spring' looks like the season but is the verb sense: to leap or skip about.
explanation.definitionFit: To caper is to leap about playfully, the same as a jump or bound.

clue.text: Sound fellow admits rising doctor's pleasant

parts.note: a toot is a short sound from a horn

indicators.note: admits means the fellow lets something in, so it goes inside

parts.note: he stands for any male person

indicators.note: in a down clue rising means the piece is read upwards, that is backwards

parts.note: MO is a medical officer, so doctor's gives MOS

explanation.surface: A healthy-sounding man takes in an up-and-coming doctor, who is pleasant company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' reverses the doctor's letters, as in a down clue they read upwards, and 'admits' puts them inside the fellow.
explanation.definitionFit: Toothsome means tasty or agreeable, hence pleasant or attractive.

clue.text: Again supply helpers in break

indicators.note: break means the letters of these words are smashed up and reassembled

explanation.surface: Fresh staff are brought in during a work break.
explanation.walkthrough: 'break' looks like a rest period, but it shuffles HELPERSIN.
explanation.definitionFit: To replenish is to fill up or restock, supplying something once more.

clue.text: Sort of biscuit to distribute at a fair

indicators.note: distribute means the letters are spread about and rearranged

explanation.surface: Biscuits are to be handed out at a fair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'distribute' rearranges ATAFAIR; 'to' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A ratafia is a small almond-flavoured macaroon-style cookie.

clue.text: Men of the church added words about crime

indicators.note: about means the postscript surrounds the crime

parts.note: PS (postscript) is words added at the end of a letter
arson is the crime of setting fires

explanation.surface: Clergymen add a few words concerning a crime.
explanation.definitionFit: Parsons are parish priests or vicars, clergymen of the church.

clue.text: A woman editor with aspiration should admit it

indicators.note: should admit means the other pieces let the word it inside them

parts.note: H is the aspirate, the breathed sound

explanation.surface: A female editor with ambitions ought to confess something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'aspiration' looks like ambition but means the breathed sound, and 'should admit' places the word it inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Edith is a female first name, so it fits a woman.

clue.text: Tense to a fault?

parts.note: a grammatical tense that, read literally, describes something not free from faults

explanation.surface: Someone is anxious to an excessive degree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tense' looks like nervous, but it is the grammar term; the past tense of unfinished action also means flawed.
explanation.definitionFit: It names a verb tense for incomplete past action and also means having faults.

clue.text: Sounds good, though in need of repair

indicators.note: sounds means the answer is spoken like the word for saintly

parts.note: holy means saintly or virtuous, that is good

explanation.surface: Something seems good even though it needs fixing.
explanation.definitionFit: Something full of holes, like worn socks, is damaged and wants mending.

clue.text: Stay and drink some ale

parts.note: to sup is to drink in sips
porter is a dark beer, a kind of ale

explanation.surface: An invitation to linger and have some beer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stay' looks like a verb but is a noun, a prop or brace.
explanation.definitionFit: A stay is a prop or brace, something that holds up a structure.

clue.text: Induce the Spanish to follow a rogue

indicators.note: to follow puts the Spanish word after the rascal

parts.note: an imp is a mischievous little rascal
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: Someone is persuaded to tag along behind a scoundrel.
explanation.definitionFit: To impel is to drive or urge someone on, to push them into action.

clue.text: "This ______ of majesty, this seat of Mars" (Richard II)

definitions.text: "This ______ of majesty, this seat of Mars" (Richard II)

parts.words: "This ______ of majesty, this seat of Mars" (Richard II)
parts.note: the missing word from John of Gaunt's speech praising England in Shakespeare's play

explanation.surface: A line quoted from Shakespeare's history play.
explanation.walkthrough: John of Gaunt's speech runs 'This royal throne of kings, this sceptred isle, This earth of majesty, this seat of Mars'.
explanation.definitionFit: The quotation completes with the word for the ground or soil of England in Gaunt's speech.

clue.text: Rash, bluff flag-captain

parts.note: to bluff someone is to fool them
Thomas Hardy was Nelson's flag captain on HMS Victory at Trafalgar

explanation.surface: A hearty captain on a flagship is reckless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bluff' looks like an adjective (hearty) but is the verb, to deceive. Hardy is famous from Nelson's dying words 'Kiss me, Hardy'.
explanation.definitionFit: Foolhardy means recklessly bold, just as rash means acting without thought.

clue.text: Spare no trouble for such a character

indicators.note: trouble means these letters are disturbed and rearranged

explanation.surface: Advice to spare no effort in playing a role.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trouble' rearranges SPARENO; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A persona is the role or character a person adopts in public or on stage.

clue.text: Newly-set tree doing badly, protective covering is called for

indicators.note: badly means these letters are poorly arranged and must be reshuffled

explanation.surface: A newly planted tree is struggling and needs some protection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Newly-set' and 'badly' both point to the anagram of TREEDOING; 'is called for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A redingote is a long double-breasted overcoat, outer garment worn against the weather.

clue.text: Cache found in south-east Mediterranean island

parts.note: SE is the compass abbreviation for south-east
Crete is the large Greek island in the Mediterranean

explanation.surface: A hoard has been discovered in the south-eastern part of a Mediterranean island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cache' looks like a noun but is the verb, to hide away.
explanation.definitionFit: To secrete is to hide something away, which is what caching it means.

clue.text: Young runners pay for such a bloomer

parts.note: colts are young horses, racehorses in their youth
to foot the bill is to pay it

explanation.surface: Young athletes pay for a big mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloomer' looks like a blunder but means a flowering plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Coltsfoot is a yellow-flowered weed, a plant that blooms.

clue.text: Cosmetic promotion seen in viewer screen

parts.note: the eye is the organ that views

indicators.note: seen in means the advert appears inside the word for screen

parts.note: to screen a film is to show it
ad, an advertisement, is a promotion

explanation.surface: An advert for a beauty product appears on a viewer's screen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seen in' puts the promotion inside the word for screen, making the dark patch that follows the viewer.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a coloured make-up product brushed on the eyelids.

clue.text: Military personnel with uniform to put right

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British army corps
dress is a uniform, as in full dress

explanation.surface: Soldiers in uniform set out to correct a wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: To redress is to remedy or set right a wrong.

clue.text: A little nourishment to be taken before study

indicators.note: to be taken before puts the food ahead of the study

parts.note: soup is a nourishing food
to con is to study or learn by heart

explanation.surface: A small meal is eaten before one sits down to study.
explanation.definitionFit: A soupcon is a tiny amount, a trace or touch of something.

clue.text: The head's about to hire painter's equipment

indicators.note: about means the head goes round the word for hire

parts.note: pate is an old word for the head
to let is to hire out

explanation.surface: The headmaster is about to engage a painter's kit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about to' reads as 'going to', but 'about' is the container sign.
explanation.definitionFit: A palette is the board on which an artist mixes colours.

clue.text: Pops round about temporary accommodation and registers

indicators.note: round about means the fathers surround the shelter

parts.note: pa is a word for father, so pops gives PAS
a tent is a temporary shelter

explanation.surface: Dads gather round a tent while registering something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pops' looks like a verb but means fathers.
explanation.definitionFit: To patent is to register an invention officially, securing rights to it.

clue.text: Discover blunder and so make complaint

parts.note: to find is to discover
a fault is a mistake or blunder

explanation.surface: Spotting a mistake leads someone to grumble.
explanation.definitionFit: To find fault is to criticise or carp, to complain.

clue.text: Sweet? Nonsense!

explanation.surface: Someone dismisses a sweet as rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is a soft toffee-like confection; the other is an exclamation meaning rubbish or humbug.

clue.text: Disrespectful man bound over — a hothead

indicators.note: over means the bound labourer is turned round

parts.note: a serf was a labourer bound to the land
the head of hot is its first letter

explanation.surface: A rude man in bonds is tied up by a hotheaded person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns SERF to FRES; 'a hothead' gives the head of 'hot', H.
explanation.definitionFit: Fresh, said of someone's manner, means cheeky or impudent.

clue.text: Keep quiet about much inertia .

indicators.note: about means the call for quiet goes round the word for much

parts.note: sh is the call for silence
a lot means much

explanation.surface: Say nothing about how much idleness there is.
explanation.definitionFit: Sloth is laziness or sluggishness, a lack of energy.

clue.text: The ear-shell some poor mermaid lost

indicators.note: some means only part of these words is taken

explanation.surface: A poor mermaid has lost her ear-shell.
explanation.walkthrough: The ear-shell, or abalone, is a shellfish found in the Channel Islands.
explanation.definitionFit: The ormer is an edible sea mollusc also called abalone or sea-ear.

clue.text: … as the workshy individual can create quite a buzz

explanation.surface: The previous clue continues: a lazy person can stir up excitement.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links to 23 across; 'quite a buzz' suggests excitement but means a humming noise.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is an idle hanger-on, like the male bee; the other is to hum monotonously.

clue.text: Cheat set up as agreed

parts.note: to con is to cheat or swindle
formed means established or set up

explanation.surface: A fraud was established, as arranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Conformed means complied or fell in line, i.e. agreed.

clue.text: The plane's moving some animals

indicators.note: moving means the letters are shifted into a new order

parts.note: plane's is taken as planes, its letters used in full

explanation.surface: An aircraft carries a load of animals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving' rearranges THEPLANES.
explanation.definitionFit: Elephants are large animals, so they are examples of creatures.

clue.text: Project to cause confusion

explanation.surface: A plan meant to sow confusion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Project' looks like a noun but is the verb, to hurl.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is to hurl something; the other is to disconcert someone.
